A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Projected Coupled Diffusion work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on multi-robot navigation, PushT manipulation and paired-face generation, including quantitative results, runtime measurements and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds numerical verification of PCD special cases and a PushT sampling-step ablation.

M1.justification: Section 6 newly describes optional inference modifications: less frequent projection, approximate intermediate projections and ADMM warm starts. These are proposed refinements; the core update equations and Algorithms 1–4 remain unchanged, and the reported experiments do not establish adoption of these options.

E1.justification: The corridor toy problem, four navigation environments, PushT task and paired-face generation coverage are retained. The new studies vary special-case configurations and sampling budgets within existing coverage, without introducing a new dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: The new Appendix C.1 comparison evaluates degenerate PCD against separately implemented classifier guidance and projected diffusion. Comparator membership in the retained robotics and image-generation experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 introduces a 200-bin, one-million-sample distribution comparison using JS, TV and L2 metrics. Appendix C.5 adds seven sampling budgets from 15 to 100 steps, using a different pretrained checkpoint, 10 initial conditions and 50 trajectory pairs per condition. These are additional protocols; existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds empirical checks that PCD reproduces CG and PD under special-case settings, plus a PushT ablation testing sensitivity to sampling-step count. Existing coupling-strength, noise-scaling and latent-interpolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies two Gaussian reference samples generated with different random seeds to contextualize stochastic distributional discrepancies. Existing standard-deviation and error-bar reporting is unchanged; no increase in repeated runs for the original experiments is reported.

E6.justification: All 15 tables from v2 retain identical numerical data. New Table 4 reports PCD–CG and PCD–PD JS divergences of 3.91×10^-5 and 5.23×10^-5, respectively. New Figure 23 reports sampling-budget-dependent diversity, constraint satisfaction and task completion under the additional checkpoint setting.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds an explicit qualification allowing the continuously differentiable coupling-cost assumption to be relaxed to costs possessing subgradients. The mathematical updates, ADMM derivations and special-case reductions are retained; the new numerical checks do not add a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: test-time joint generation through coupling and projection, hard-constraint enforcement and generalization of existing guidance methods without retraining. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's existing fidelity, runtime and interpolation caveats, Section 6 adds a general warning about constraints conflicting with learned-distribution support and discusses practical mitigations. Appendix C.5 explains misleading diversity scores from poor low-step trajectories and proposes more accurate posterior estimates as an explanation for benefits at larger sampling budgets.

D1.justification: The added studies document their configurations, including the separate 100-step-trained checkpoint used only for the new PushT ablation. The reproducibility statement replaces supplementary-material and future code/weight-release wording with the repository already linked in v2; it does not establish newly available code. Existing hardware and solver details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting discussion of manifold constraints, derivative-free guidance, constrained planning and proximal algorithms. It removes the footnote distinguishing Liang et al. (2025) while retaining that citation. The main related-work organization and research positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 adds a limitations section, two appendix study sections, numbered appendix subheadings and acknowledgments, and updates the publication header and reproducibility statement. Existing prose receives limited editing rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4 and Figures 11 and 23. Existing appendix displays are relocated and regrouped, including Figures 8–10 nearer their discussion and the paired-face examples together. Retained tables and figures largely preserve their display structure.

improvement.justification: The special-case verification and sampling-step ablation add useful supporting evidence, while the new limitations and low-step failure interpretation clarify when results are meaningful. The distinct ablation checkpoint is explicitly disclosed. These improve transparency and validation without changing the main empirical findings; the proposed runtime shortcuts remain unevaluated, limiting the strength of the improvement.
